ip_top_stories.title: Hachette Gets AI Book Cover IP Claims Tossed, For Now
ip_top_stories.summary: A court has dismissed Hachette's intellectual property claims related to AI-generated book covers, though the ruling appears to leave open the possibility of refiling. The case is an early test of how traditional publishing IP claims fare against AI image generation in a litigation context.

ip_top_stories.title: Meta Generative AI Copyright Ruling Fails to Get Quick Appeal
ip_top_stories.summary: A federal court has declined to grant Meta an expedited appeal in a generative AI copyright case, meaning the litigation will continue on its current track. The ruling keeps alive one of the higher-profile cases examining whether training large language models on copyrighted content constitutes infringement.

ip_top_stories.title: AI companies' pitch of creatives-focused fund faces pushback in copyright law impasse
ip_top_stories.summary: AI companies have proposed establishing a fund directed at creative industries as a potential resolution to the ongoing copyright impasse, but the offer is facing resistance from rights holders and policymakers. The pushback reflects broader scepticism about voluntary compensation mechanisms as a substitute for legislative or judicial resolution.

ip_top_stories.title: Midjourney asks court to expose Hollywood studios' AI practices
ip_top_stories.summary: Midjourney has filed a court request seeking to compel Hollywood studios to disclose their own internal use of AI tools, as part of its defence in an ongoing copyright dispute. The move seeks to surface potential inconsistencies between studios' litigation stance and their operational AI adoption.

ip_top_stories.title: After a judge denied Sony's move to expand its Udio case, Suno asks court to reject UMG and Sony's bid to add 61K recordings
ip_top_stories.summary: Following a judge's refusal to allow Sony to expand its case against AI music generator Udio, Suno is now asking the court to similarly reject a bid by Universal Music Group and Sony to add 61,000 additional recordings to their lawsuit. The development signals escalating disputes over the scope of AI music copyright litigation.

ip_further_links.title: Hollywood's AI habits become courtroom evidence
ip_further_links.summary: Studios' internal use of AI tools is increasingly being surfaced as evidence in copyright litigation, complicating their position as plaintiffs in cases against AI companies.

ip_further_links.title: Roc Nation Accuses Opposing Counsel of Using AI-Generated Fake Quotes in Fat Joe Case
ip_further_links.summary: Roc Nation has accused opposing counsel of submitting AI-generated fabricated quotes in filings related to the Fat Joe lawsuit, raising serious professional conduct concerns around AI use in legal proceedings.

ip_further_links.title: AI giants' copyright olive branch rejected by industry, government
ip_further_links.summary: Proposals from major AI companies to offer concessions to creative industries on copyright have been rejected by both rights holders and government representatives.

ip_further_links.title: AI Is Eating the Book World
ip_further_links.summary: A broader examination of how AI is disrupting the publishing industry, covering training data use, content generation, and the implications for authors and publishers.

ip_further_links.title: Vietnam clarifies AI authorship, training data and copyright liability: A comparative lens
ip_further_links.summary: Vietnam has introduced clarifications to its copyright framework addressing AI authorship, training data use, and liability, analysed here in a comparative international context.

ip_further_links.title: Courts step in to check AI-driven breaches of personality rights
ip_further_links.summary: Courts in multiple jurisdictions are beginning to address AI-generated content that infringes personality rights, including voice and likeness, as litigation in this area accelerates.

ip_further_links.title: Labor push for law to label AI in creative works
ip_further_links.summary: Australian Labor has indicated support for legislation requiring AI-generated or AI-assisted creative works to carry disclosure labels, as part of broader policy efforts to protect the creative sector.

ip_further_links.title: IPA Congress 2026 Ends on an Optimistic Note [Metered]
ip_further_links.summary: The International Publishers Association Congress 2026 closed with a broadly optimistic tone, with discussions including AI's impact on publishing and intellectual property among the key themes.

ip_further_links.title: Who Owns the Worldview Inside an AI Model?
ip_further_links.summary: An analysis examining the unresolved question of whether the implicit values, perspectives, and knowledge structures embedded within AI models carry any intellectual property protections.

ip_further_links.title: Protecting Human Voices in the Age of AI: Australian Copyright Law and Beyond
ip_further_links.summary: An analysis of how Australian copyright law currently addresses AI-generated voice cloning and what reforms may be needed to provide adequate protection for performers.
